Does NOT touch ../captured-admission-v0/admission_check.py -- this is the profile-owned pre-validator that runs BEFORE a record reaches the shared obligation checker, per Merlini/Pavlo's fix (2026-08-02).
request_class_derivation: request_class buckets our real, live artifact_type (core/models.py, 11-valued Literal) using the SAME irreversible/reversible split already live in production (services/proof_signing.py IRREVERSIBLE_ARTIFACT_TYPES) -- not a new invented axis. long = {onchain_action, trade, sanctions_screening}; short = the other 8 real artifact_type values.
policy_sla_table: invinoveritas.review.v5: short=60s, long=180s. long is longer because irreversible-class review can trigger the reversibility_gate's extra confidence-floor check (routes/inference.py) -- real additional processing, not an arbitrary bigger number.

cases._annotation: positive vector 1/2 (Pavlo's ask): a reversible artifact_type (code_diff) buckets to request_class=short, Δ=60s, and the supplied response_deadline + deadline_policy_commitment both match what's deterministically recomputed from {policy_version, request_class, accepted_at} alone.
positive vector 2/2: an irreversible artifact_type (trade) buckets to request_class=long, Δ=180s.

negative 1/4 (Pavlo): supplied deadline differs from the derived deadline. The commitment itself is correct (isolates this failure from the commitment-mismatch case below) but the record claims response_deadline=3999 instead of the correctly-derived 3060.
negative 2/4 (Pavlo): request_class isn't one of the two buckets the SLA table actually defines.

negative 3/4 (Pavlo): the artifact_type (trade, an irreversible-class artifact that structurally buckets to 'long') doesn't match the request_class the record actually declares ('short') -- exactly the 'request_class changed after capture/admission binding' case Pavlo named. Catches an attempt to claim the cheaper short-class SLA for a long-class artifact.

negative 4/4 (Pavlo): 'later policy table used to reinterpret an older admission.' This record was correctly bound under an OLDER SLA table (short=45s, not the current 60s) -- accepted_at=6000, response_deadline=6045, commitment computed under the prior table. Evaluating it against the CURRENT live table (_use_prev_table omitted -> defaults to POLICY_SLA_TABLE) correctly rejects it at the COMMITMENT check, not just the raw number -- the deadline_policy_commitment hash is the actual cryptographic evidence of which table was pinned at accepted_at, so a reinterpretation attempt is caught even before comparing the numeric deadline. A validator that only checked the raw response_deadline number could be fooled by a coincidental match; checking the commitment can't be. This is exactly why deadline_policy_commitment is bound into the record at all, not just response_deadline itself.
